chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the free woman who is under the ownership of a slave (as his wife), and she buys him [to free him]. Does that invalidate his marriage? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he is an owned slave who has no power over anything.'
ai.seo_question: Does a free woman buying her slave husband invalidate their marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the marriage between a free woman and her slave husband is annulled upon her purchasing and freeing him, as the slave's lack of independent legal capacity (qudra) prevents him from sustaining the marital bond while in servitude. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the husband's financial and legal autonomy as a condition for the validity of the marriage contract in mixed-status unions. The hadith underscores the transformative effect of manumission on family law, linking social status directly to contractual validity.
